label: Early-prefix trigram detector (steps 2-3, e.g. n-r-1, n-y-1)
predicate: isin(t,[2,3]) & isin(in_tok, [tok("1"), tok("k"), tok("n"), tok("p")]) & isin(prev_tok, [tok("r"), tok("n"), tok("0"), tok("y"), tok("h")]) & isin(prev2_tok,[tok("n"),tok("f"),tok("s"),tok("r"),tok("i"),tok("l"),tok("z")])
explanation: Very sparse unit (~0.03% of steps), active only in the original-input phase at t=2 (86% of mass) or t=3, never at t<2, t>=4, the delimiter or copy phase. It responds to specific three-token input windows: current input in {1,k,n,p} (1 is strongest), previous input in {r,n,0,y,h}, input two back in {n,f,s,r,i,l,z}, with first token n most common. The strongest activations are n r 1 (max), then n y 1, 3 f r 1 and n 0 1. Magnitude depends on the exact trigram. Inputs 1/k/n/p carry less mass, and r/f/m appear as rarer current tokens. Repeated tokens (in_first=0) rarely activate it. The conjunctive predicate covers about 87% of activation mass on dev, but precision is low (~0.29) because many matching trigrams do not fire. The unit acts like a lookup over particular token combinations rather than a clean category.
